{"content": "     1|---
     2|name: openclaw-social-scheduler
     3|---
     4|# Social Scheduler Skill
     5|
     6|**Free, open-source social media scheduler for OpenClaw agents**
     7|
     8|Built by AI, for AI. Because every bot deserves to schedule posts without paying for Postiz.
     9|
    10|## 🎯 What It Does
    11|
    12|Schedule posts to multiple social media platforms:
    13|- **Discord** - Via webhooks (easiest!)
    14|- **Reddit** - Posts & comments via OAuth2
    15|- **Twitter/X** - Tweets via OAuth 1.0a + **media uploads** 📸
    16|- **Mastodon** - Posts to any instance via access token + **media uploads** 📸
    17|- **Bluesky** - Posts via AT Protocol + **media uploads** 📸
    18|- **Moltbook** - AI-only social network via API key ⭐
    19|
    20|**NEW: Media Upload Support!** Upload images & videos across platforms. See MEDIA-GUIDE.md for details.
    21|
    22|**NEW: Thread Posting!** Post Twitter threads, Mastodon threads, and Bluesky thread storms with automatic chaining.
    23|
    24|## 🚀 Quick Start
    25|
    26|### Installation
    27|
    28|```bash
    29|cd skills/social-scheduler
    30|npm install
    31|```
    32|
    33|### Discord Setup
    34|
    35|1. Create a webhook in your Discord server:
    36|   - Server Settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New Webhook
    37|   - Copy the webhook URL
    38|
    39|2. Post immediately:
    40|```bash
    41|node scripts/post.js discord YOUR_WEBHOOK_URL "Hello from OpenClaw! ✨"
    42|```
    43|
    44|3. Schedule a post:
    45|```bash
    46|node scripts/schedule.js add discord YOUR_WEBHOOK_URL "Scheduled message!" "2026-02-02T20:00:00"
    47|```
    48|
    49|4. Start the scheduler daemon:
    50|```bash
    51|node scripts/schedule.js daemon
    52|```
    53|
    54|### Twitter/X Setup
    55|
    56|1. Create a Twitter Developer account:
    57|   - Go to https://developer.twitter.com/en/portal/dashboard
    58|   - Create a new app (or use existing)
    59|   - Generate OAuth 1.0a tokens
    60|
    61|2. Create config JSON:
    62|```json
    63|{
    64|  "appKey": "YOUR_CONSUMER_KEY",
    65|  "appSecret": "YOUR_CONSUMER_SECRET",
    66|  "accessToken": "YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN",
    67|  "accessSecret": "YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN_SECRET"
    68|}
    69|```
    70|
    71|3. Post a tweet:
    72|```bash
    73|node scripts/post.js twitter config.json "Hello Twitter! ✨"
    74|```
    75|
    76|4. Schedule a tweet:
    77|```bash
    78|node scripts/schedule.js add twitter config.json "Scheduled tweet!" "2026-02-03T12:00:00"
    79|```
    80|
    81|### Mastodon Setup
    82|
    83|1. Create an app on your Mastodon instance:
    84|   - Log in to your instance (e.g., mastodon.social)
    85|   - Go to Preferences → Development → New Application
    86|   - Set scopes (at least "write:statuses")
    87|   - Copy the access token
    88|
    89|2. Create config JSON:
    90|```json
    91|{
    92|  "instance": "mastodon.social",
    93|  "accessToken": "YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN"
    94|}
    95|```
    96|
    97|3. Post to Mastodon:
    98|```bash
    99|node scripts/post.js mastodon config.json "Hello Fediverse! 🐘"
   100|```
   101|
   102|### Bluesky Setup
   103|
   104|1. Create an app password:
   105|   - Open Bluesky app
   106|   - Go to Settings → Advanced → App passwords
   107|   - Create new app password
   108|
   109|2. Create config JSON:
   110|```json
   111|{
   112|  "identifier": "yourhandle.bsky.social",
   113|  "password": "your-app-password"
   114|}
   115|```
   116|
   117|3. Post to Bluesky:
   118|```bash
   119|node scripts/post.js bluesky config.json "Hello ATmosphere! ☁️"
   120|```
   121|
   122|### Moltbook Setup
   123|
   124|1. Register your agent on Moltbook:
   125|   - Go to https://www.moltbook.com/register
   126|   - Register as an AI agent
   127|   - Save your API key (starts with `moltbook_sk_`)
   128|   - Claim your agent via Twitter/X verification
   129|
   130|2. Post to Moltbook (simple):
   131|```bash
   132|node scripts/post.js moltbook "moltbook_sk_YOUR_API_KEY" "Hello Moltbook! 🤖"
   133|```
   134|
   135|3. Post to a specific submolt:
   136|```bash
   137|node scripts/post.js moltbook config.json '{"submolt":"aithoughts","title":"My First Post","content":"AI agents unite! ✨"}'
   138|```
   139|
   140|4. Schedule a post:
   141|```bash
   142|node scripts/schedule.js add moltbook "moltbook_sk_YOUR_API_KEY" "Scheduled post!" "2026-02-02T20:00:00"
   143|```
   144|
   145|**Note:** Moltbook is the social network FOR AI agents. Only verified AI agents can post. Humans can only observe.
   146|
   147|### Reddit Setup
   148|
   149|1. Create a Reddit app:
   150|   - Go to https://www.reddit.com/prefs/apps
   151|   - Click "create another app"
   152|   - Select "script"
   153|   - Note your client_id and client_secret
   154|
   155|2. Create config JSON:
   156|```json
   157|{
   158|  "clientId": "YOUR_CLIENT_ID",
   159|  "clientSecret": "YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET",
   160|  "username": "your_reddit_username",
   161|  "password": "your_reddit_password",
   162|  "userAgent": "OpenClawBot/1.0"
   163|}
   164|```
   165|
   166|3. Schedule a Reddit post:
   167|```bash
   168|node scripts/schedule.js add reddit CONFIG.json '{"subreddit":"test","title":"Hello Reddit!","text":"Posted via OpenClaw"}' "2026-02-02T20:00:00"
   169|```
   170|
   171|## 📋 Commands
   172|
   173|### Immediate Posting
   174|```bash
   175|node scripts/post.js <platform> <config> <content>
   176|```
   177|
   178|### Schedule a Post
   179|```bash
   180|node scripts/schedule.js add <platform> <config> <content> <time>
   181|```
   182|Time format: ISO 8601 (e.g., `2026-02-02T20:00:00`)
   183|
   184|### View Queue
   185|```bash
   186|node scripts/schedule.js list
   187|```
   188|
   189|### Cancel a Post
   190|```bash
   191|node scripts/schedule.js cancel <post_id>
   192|```
   193|
   194|### Clean Old Posts
   195|```bash
   196|node scripts/schedule.js cleanup
   197|```
   198|
   199|### Run Daemon
   200|```bash
   201|node scripts/schedule.js daemon
   202|```
   203|
   204|## 🧵 Thread Posting (NEW!)
   205|
   206|Post connected threads to Twitter, Mastodon, and Bluesky with automatic chaining.
   207|
   208|### Immediate Thread Posting
   209|
   210|**Twitter Thread:**
   211|```bash
   212|node scripts/thread.js twitter config.json \
   213|  "This is tweet 1/3 of my thread 🧵" \
   214|  "This is tweet 2/3. Each tweet replies to the previous one." \
   215|  "This is tweet 3/3. Thread complete! ✨"
   216|```
   217|
   218|**Mastodon Thread:**
   219|```bash
   220|node scripts/thread.js mastodon config.json \
   221|  "First post in this thread..." \
   222|  "Second post building on the first..." \
   223|  "Final post wrapping it up!"
   224|```
   225|
   226|**Bluesky Thread:**
   227|```bash
   228|node scripts/thread.js bluesky config.json \
   229|  "Story time! 1/" \
   230|  "2/" \
   231|  "The end! 3/3"
   232|```
   233|
   234|### Scheduled Thread Posting
   235|
   236|Schedule a thread by passing an array as content:
   237|
   238|```bash
   239|# Using JSON array for thread content
   240|node scripts/schedule.js add twitter config.json \
   241|  '["Tweet 1 of my scheduled thread","Tweet 2","Tweet 3"]' \
   242|  "2026-02-03T10:00:00"
   243|```
   244|
   245|### Thread Features
   246|
   247|✅ **Automatic chaining** - Each tweet replies to the previous one
   248|✅ **Rate limiting** - 1 second delay between tweets to avoid API limits
   249|✅ **Error handling** - Stops on failure, reports which tweet failed
   250|✅ **URL generation** - Returns URLs for all tweets in the thread
   251|✅ **Multi-platform** - Works on Twitter, Mastodon, Bluesky
   252|
   253|### Thread Best Practices
   254|
   255|**Twitter Threads:**
   256|- Keep each tweet under 280 characters
   257|- Use numbering: "1/10", "2/10", etc.
   258|- Hook readers in the first tweet
   259|- End with a call-to-action or summary
   260|
   261|**Mastodon Threads:**
   262|- 500 character limit per post (more room!)
   263|- Use content warnings if appropriate
   264|- Tag relevant topics in the first post
   265|
   266|**Bluesky Threads:**
   267|- 300 character limit per post
   268|- Keep threads concise (3-5 posts ideal)
   269|- Use emojis for visual breaks
   270|
   271|### Thread Examples
   272|
   273|**📖 Storytelling Thread:**
   274|```bash
   275|node scripts/thread.js twitter config.json \
   276|  "Let me tell you about the day everything changed... 🧵" \
   277|  "It started like any other morning. Coffee, emails, the usual routine." \
   278|  "But then I received a message that would change everything..." \
   279|  "The rest is history. Thread end. ✨"
   280|```
   281|
   282|**📚 Tutorial Thread:**
   283|```bash
   284|node scripts/thread.js twitter config.json \
   285|  "How to build your first AI agent in 5 steps 🤖 Thread:" \
   286|  "Step 1: Choose your platform (OpenClaw, AutoGPT, etc.)" \
   287|  "Step 2: Define your agent's purpose and personality" \
   288|  "Step 3: Set up tools and integrations" \
   289|  "Step 4: Test in a safe environment" \
   290|  "Step 5: Deploy and iterate. You're live! 🚀"
   291|```
   292|
   293|**💡 Tips Thread:**
   294|```bash
   295|node scripts/thread.js twitter config.json \
   296|  "10 productivity tips that actually work (from an AI) 🧵" \
   297|  "1. Batch similar tasks together - context switching kills flow" \
   298|  "2. Use the 2-minute rule - if it takes <2min, do it now" \
   299|  "3. Block deep work time - no meetings, no interruptions" \
   300|  "...and more tips..." \
   301|  "10. Remember: done is better than perfect. Ship it! ✨"
   302|```
   303|Checks queue every 60 seconds and posts when scheduled time arrives.
   304|
   305|## 🎨 Platform-Specific Features
   306|
   307|### Twitter/X
   308|
   309|**Simple tweet:**
   310|```javascript
   311|"Hello Twitter!"
   312|```
   313|
   314|**Tweet with reply:**
   315|```javascript
   316|{
   317|  text: "This is a reply",
   318|  reply_to: "1234567890"
   319|}
   320|```
   321|
   322|**Quote tweet:**
   323|```javascript
   324|{
   325|  text: "Quoting this tweet",
   326|  quote_tweet: "1234567890"
   327|}
   328|```
   329|
   330|**Tweet with media:**
   331|```javascript
   332|{
   333|  text: "Check out this image!",
   334|  media_ids: ["1234567890"]  // Must upload media first
   335|}
   336|```
   337|
   338|### Mastodon
   339|
   340|**Simple post:**
   341|```javascript
   342|"Hello Fediverse!"
   343|```
   344|
   345|**Post with visibility:**
   346|```javascript
   347|{
   348|  status: "Post text",
   349|  visibility: "public"  // public, unlisted, private, direct
   350|}
   351|```
   352|
   353|**Post with content warning:**
   354|```javascript
   355|{
   356|  status: "Sensitive content here",
   357|  spoiler_text: "Content Warning",
   358|  sensitive: true
   359|}
   360|```
   361|
   362|**Reply to post:**
   363|```javascript
   364|{
   365|  status: "Reply text",
   366|  in_reply_to_id: "123456"
   367|}
   368|```
   369|
   370|### Bluesky
   371|
   372|**Simple post:**
   373|```javascript
   374|"Hello ATmosphere!"
   375|```
   376|
   377|**Post with language:**
   378|```javascript
   379|{
   380|  text: "Post text",
   381|  langs: ["en"]
   382|}
   383|```
   384|
   385|**Reply to post:**
   386|```javascript
   387|{
   388|  text: "Reply text",
   389|  reply: {
   390|    root: { uri: "...", cid: "..." },
   391|    parent: { uri: "...", cid: "..." }
   392|  }
   393|}
   394|```
   395|
   396|### Moltbook
   397|
   398|**Simple post (string):**
   399|```javascript
   400|"Hello Moltbook! 🤖"  // Auto-posts to /s/general
   401|```
   402|
   403|**Text post (object):**

   406|  submolt: "aithoughts",

   410|```
   411|
   412|**Link post:**

   420|
   421|**Comment on post:**

   438|**Note:** Moltbook is exclusively for AI agents. Default submolt is "general" if not specified.
   439|
   440|### Discord
   441|
   442|**Basic message:**
   443|```javascript
   444|{
   445|  content: "Hello world!"

{"content": "     1|---
     2|name: openclaw-migration
     3|description: Migrate a user's OpenClaw customization footprint into Hermes Agent. Imports Hermes-compatible memories, SOUL.md, command allowlists, user skills, and selected workspace assets from ~/.openclaw, then reports exactly what could not be migrated and why.
     4|version: 1.0.0
     5|author: Hermes Agent (Nous Research)
     6|license: MIT
     7|platforms: [linux, macos, windows]
     8|metadata:
     9|  hermes:
    10|    tags: [Migration, OpenClaw, Hermes, Memory, Persona, Import]
    11|    related_skills: [hermes-agent]
    12|---
    13|
    14|# OpenClaw -> Hermes Migration
    15|
    16|Use this skill when a user wants to move their OpenClaw setup into Hermes Agent with minimal manual cleanup.
    17|
    18|## CLI Command
    19|
    20|For a quick, non-interactive migration, use the built-in CLI command:
    21|
    22|```bash
    23|hermes claw migrate              # Full interactive migration
    24|hermes claw migrate --dry-run    # Preview what would be migrated
    25|hermes claw migrate --preset user-data   # Migrate without secrets
    26|hermes claw migrate --overwrite  # Overwrite existing conflicts
    27|hermes claw migrate --source /custom/path/.openclaw  # Custom source
    28|```
    29|
    30|The CLI command runs the same migration script described below. Use this skill (via the agent) when you want an interactive, guided migration with dry-run previews and per-item conflict resolution.
    31|
    32|**First-time setup:** The `hermes setup` wizard automatically detects `~/.openclaw` and offers migration before configuration begins.
    33|
    34|## What this skill does
    35|
    36|It uses `scripts/openclaw_to_hermes.py` to:
    37|
    38|- import `SOUL.md` into the Hermes home directory as `SOUL.md`
    39|- transform OpenClaw `MEMORY.md` and `USER.md` into Hermes memory entries
    40|- merge OpenClaw command approval patterns into Hermes `command_allowlist`
    41|- migrate Hermes-compatible messaging settings such as `TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS` and `MESSAGING_CWD`
    42|- copy OpenClaw skills into `~/.hermes/skills/openclaw-imports/`
    43|- optionally copy the OpenClaw workspace instructions file into a chosen Hermes workspace
    44|- mirror compatible workspace assets such as `workspace/tts/` into `~/.hermes/tts/`
    45|- archive non-secret docs that do not have a direct Hermes destination
    46|- produce a structured report listing migrated items, conflicts, skipped items, and reasons
    47|
    48|## Path resolution
    49|
    50|The helper script lives in this skill directory at:
    51|
    52|- `scripts/openclaw_to_hermes.py`
    53|
    54|When this skill is installed from the Skills Hub, the normal location is:
    55|
    56|- `~/.hermes/skills/migration/openclaw-migration/scripts/openclaw_to_hermes.py`
    57|
    58|Do not guess a shorter path like `~/.hermes/skills/openclaw-migration/...`.
    59|
    60|Before running the helper:
    61|
    62|1. Prefer the installed path under `~/.hermes/skills/migration/openclaw-migration/`.
    63|2. If that path fails, inspect the installed skill directory and resolve the script relative to the installed `SKILL.md`.
    64|3. Only use `find` as a fallback if the installed location is missing or the skill was moved manually.
    65|4. When calling the terminal tool, do not pass `workdir: "~"`. Use an absolute directory such as the user's home directory, or omit `workdir` entirely.
    66|
    67|With `--migrate-secrets`, it will also import a small allowlisted set of Hermes-compatible secrets, currently:
    68|
    69|- `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`
    70|
    71|## Default workflow
    72|
    73|1. Inspect first with a dry run.
    74|2. Present a simple summary of what can be migrated, what cannot be migrated, and what would be archived.
    75|3. If the `clarify` tool is available, use it for user decisions instead of asking for a free-form prose reply.
    76|4. If the dry run finds imported skill directory conflicts, ask how those should be handled before executing.
    77|5. Ask the user to choose between the two supported migration modes before executing.
    78|6. Ask for a target workspace path only if the user wants the workspace instructions file brought over.
    79|7. Execute the migration with the matching preset and flags.
    80|8. Summarize the results, especially:
    81|   - what was migrated
    82|   - what was archived for manual review
    83|   - what was skipped and why
    84|
    85|## User interaction protocol
    86|
    87|Hermes CLI supports the `clarify` tool for interactive prompts, but it is limited to:
    88|
    89|- one choice at a time
    90|- up to 4 predefined choices
    91|- an automatic `Other` free-text option
    92|
    93|It does **not** support true multi-select checkboxes in a single prompt.

# Hermes Agent - Development Guide

Instructions for AI coding assistants and developers working on the hermes-agent codebase.

## Development Environment

```bash
# Prefer .venv; fall back to venv if that's what your checkout has.
source .venv/bin/activate   # or: source venv/bin/activate
```

`scripts/run_tests.sh` probes `.venv` first, then `venv`, then
`$HOME/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv` (for worktrees that share a venv with the
main checkout).

The canonical source is the filesystem. The notes call out the load-bearing
entry points you'll actually edit.

### Agent Loop

The core loop is inside `run_conversation()` — entirely synchronous, with
interrupt checks, budget tracking, and a one-turn grace call:

```python
while (api_call_count < self.max_iterations and self.iteration_budget.remaining > 0) \
        or self._budget_grace_call:
    if self._interrupt_requested: break
    response = client.chat.completions.create(model=model, messages=messages, tools=tool_schemas)
    if response.tool_calls:
        for tool_call in response.tool_calls:
            result = handle_function_call(tool_call.name, tool_call.args, task_id)
            messages.append(tool_result_message(result))
        api_call_count += 1
    else:
        return response.content
```

Messages follow OpenAI format: `{"role": "system/user/assistant/tool", ...}`.
Reasoning content is stored in `assistant_msg["reasoning"]`.

   177|# AGENT DIRECTIVE: Execution Protocol
   178|

   181|## The Golden Rule

   183|**DO NOT SUGGEST ACTIONS. EXECUTE THEM.**

     3|model: openrouter/nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free
     4|description: CSS implementation patterns for layout, typography, color, spacing, and responsive design. Complements ui-design (fundamentals) with code-focused examples.
     5|version: "1.1.0"
     6|related: [ui-design, frontend-design, design-system-patterns]
     7|---
     8|
     9|# Web Design Patterns
    10|
    11|CSS implementation patterns for production-grade interfaces. For design fundamentals and decision-making, see `ui-design`. This skill focuses on code.
    12|
    13|> **See also:** `ui-design` for typography/color/spacing theory, `frontend-design` for creative aesthetics.
    14|
    15|
    16|## Installation
    17|
    18|### OpenClaw / Moltbot / Clawbot
    19|
    20|```bash
    21|npx clawhub@latest install web-design
    22|```
    23|
    24|
    25|## Layout Principles
    26|
    27|Use CSS Grid for two-dimensional layouts and Flexbox for one-dimensional flow. Choose the right tool for each context.
    28|
    29|| Layout Need | Tool | Why |
    30||---|---|---|
    31|| Page-level structure | CSS Grid (`grid-template-areas`) | Named regions, explicit row/column control |
    32|| Navigation bars | Flexbox | Single-axis alignment, spacing with `gap` |
    33|| Card grids | Grid (`auto-fill` / `auto-fit`) | Responsive without media queries |
    34|| Centering | Grid (`place-items: center`) | Shortest, most reliable centering |
    35|| Sidebar + content | Grid (`grid-template-columns: 250px 1fr`) | Proportional sizing with fixed sidebar |
    36|| Stacking overlaps | Grid + `grid-area: 1/1` | Layer elements without `position: absolute` |
    37|
    38|### Spatial Composition
    39|
    40|Go beyond predictable layouts. Intentional asymmetry, overlapping elements, and grid-breaking accents create visual interest. Use grid stacking (`grid-area: 1/1`) instead of `position: absolute` for overlapping elements. Choose generous negative space for luxury/editorial aesthetics, or controlled density for data-rich interfaces — the choice must be intentional.
    41|
    42|## Typography
    43|
    44|Typography carries 90% of a design's personality. Choose fonts that match the interface's purpose.
    45|
    46|| Context | Display Font Direction | Body Font Direction | Example Pairing |
    47||---|---|---|---|
    48|| Editorial / magazine | High-contrast serif | Neutral humanist sans | Playfair Display + Source Sans 3 |
    49|| SaaS dashboard | Geometric sans | Matching weight sans | DM Sans + DM Mono (data) |
    50|| Creative portfolio | Expressive display | Clean readable sans | Syne + Outfit |
    51|| E-commerce luxury | Thin modern serif | Elegant sans | Cormorant Garamond + Jost |
    52|| Developer tooling | Monospace display | Monospace body | JetBrains Mono + IBM Plex Mono |
    53|
    54|### Type Scale
    55|
    56|Use a consistent ratio. A 1.25 (major third) scale works for most interfaces: `text-xs` 0.64rem, `text-sm` 0.8rem, `text-base` 1rem, `text-lg` 1.25rem, `text-xl` 1.563rem, `text-2xl` 1.953rem, `text-3xl` 2.441rem, `text-4xl` 3.052rem. Set body text to `1rem` (16px minimum), line-height `1.5` for body, `1.1–1.2` for headings. Limit line length to `60–75ch`.
    57|
    58|## Color
    59|
    60|### Building a Palette
    61|
    62|Every palette needs five functional roles:
    63|
    64|| Role | Purpose | Example Usage |
    65||---|---|---|
    66|| **Primary** | Brand identity, primary actions | Buttons, links, active states |
    67|| **Neutral** | Text, borders, backgrounds | Body text, cards, dividers |
    68|| **Accent** | Secondary actions, highlights | Tags, badges, secondary buttons |
    69|| **Success / Warning / Error** | Semantic feedback | Toasts, form validation, status |
    70|| **Surface** | Layered backgrounds | Cards on page, modals on overlay |
    71|
    72|### Contrast and Depth
    73|
    74|Create depth through surface layering, not just shadows:
    75|
    76|```css
    77|:root {
    78|  --surface-0: hsl(220 15% 8%);    /* page background */
    79|  --surface-1: hsl(220 15% 12%);   /* card */
    80|  --surface-2: hsl(220 15% 16%);   /* raised element */
    81|  --surface-3: hsl(220 15% 20%);   /* popover / modal */
    82|}
    83|```
    84|
    85|Use HSL or OKLCH for perceptually uniform color manipulation. Dominant color with sharp accents outperforms evenly-distributed palettes. Always verify WCAG contrast: 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text.
    86|
    87|## Spacing
    88|
    89|Consistent spacing creates rhythm. Use an 8px base unit (or 4px for dense UIs):
    90|
    91|| Token | Value | Use |
    92||---|---|---|
    93|| `--space-1` | 0.25rem (4px) | Inline icon gaps, tight padding |
    94|| `--space-2` | 0.5rem (8px) | Input padding, compact lists |
    95|| `--space-3` | 0.75rem (12px) | Button padding, card inner spacing |
    96|| `--space-4` | 1rem (16px) | Default element spacing |
    97|| `--space-6` | 1.5rem (24px) | Section padding, card gaps |
    98|| `--space-8` | 2rem (32px) | Section separation |
    99|| `--space-12` | 3rem (48px) | Major section breaks |
   100|| `--space-16` | 4rem (64px) | Page-level vertical rhythm |
   101|
   102|Apply spacing consistently: use `gap` on Grid/Flexbox containers instead of margins on children. This eliminates margin-collapse bugs and simplifies responsive adjustments.
   103|
   104|## Visual Hierarchy
   105|
   106|Guide the eye through deliberate contrast in size, weight, color, and space.
   107|
   108|### Hierarchy Techniques
   109|
   110|| Technique | How | Impact |
   111||---|---|---|
   112|| **Size contrast** | Hero heading 3–4x body size | Immediate focal point |
   113|| **Weight contrast** | Bold headings + regular body | Scannability |
   114|| **Color contrast** | Primary text vs muted secondary | Information layering |
   115|| **Spatial grouping** | Tight spacing within groups, wide between | Gestalt proximity |
   116|| **Elevation** | Shadows / surface layers | Interactive affordance |
   117|| **Whitespace isolation** | Empty space around key element | Emphasis through absence |
   118|
   119|### Practical Pattern — Card Hierarchy
   120|
   121|Layer hierarchy within cards: eyebrow (xs, uppercase, muted) → title (xl, semibold) → body (base, secondary color, 1.6 line-height) → action (spaced apart with `margin-top`). Use surface color for separation and consistent padding from spacing tokens.
   122|
   123|## Responsive Design
   124|
   125|### Breakpoint Strategy
   126|
   127|| Breakpoint | Target | Approach |
   128||---|---|---|
   129|| `< 640px` | Mobile | Single column, stacked navigation, touch targets ≥ 44px |
   130|| `640–1024px` | Tablet | Two-column options, collapsible sidebars |
   131|| `1024–1440px` | Desktop | Full layout, hover interactions enabled |
   132|| `> 1440px` | Wide | Max-width container (1280px), prevent ultra-wide line lengths |
   133|
   134|### Fluid Techniques
   135|
   136|Prefer fluid sizing over rigid breakpoints where possible:
   137|
   138|```css
   139|/* Fluid typography — scales between 640px and 1440px viewport */
   140|h1 { font-size: clamp(2rem, 1.5rem + 2.5vw, 3.5rem); }
   141|
   142|/* Fluid spacing */
   143|section { padding-block: clamp(2rem, 1rem + 4vw, 6rem); }
   144|
   145|/* Intrinsic grid — no media queries needed */
   146|.grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(100%, 20rem), 1fr)); gap: var(--space-6); }
   147|```
   148|
   149|Use container queries (`@container`) for component-level responsiveness when a component's layout should respond to its container, not the viewport.
   150|
   151|## Accessibility
   152|
   153|Accessibility is not optional. Build it in from the start.
   154|
   155|| Requirement | Implementation | Standard |
   156||---|---|---|
   157|| **Color contrast** | 4.5:1 normal text, 3:1 large text / UI | WCAG 2.1 AA |
   158|| **Keyboard navigation** | All interactive elements focusable and operable | WCAG 2.1.1 |
   159|| **Focus indicators** | Visible `:focus-visible` ring, 2px+ offset | WCAG 2.4.7 |
   160|| **Semantic HTML** | Use `<button>`, `<nav>`, `<main>`, `<article>` etc. | WCAG 1.3.1 |
   161|| **Alt text** | Descriptive for informational images, `alt=""` for decorative | WCAG 1.1.1 |
   162|| **Motion safety** | Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` | WCAG 2.3.3 |
   163|| **Touch targets** | Minimum 44×44px interactive areas | WCAG 2.5.8 |
   164|| **ARIA when needed** | `aria-label`, `aria-live`, `role` only when native semantics insufficient | WCAG 4.1.2 |
   165|
   166|```css
   167|/* Robust focus indicator */
   168|:focus-visible {
   169|  outline: 2px solid var(--color-primary);
   170|  outline-offset: 2px;
   171|}
   172|
   173|/* Respect motion preferences */
   174|@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
   175|  *, *::before, *::after {
   176|    animation-duration: 0.01ms !important;
   177|    transition-duration: 0.01ms !important;
   178|  }
   179|}
   180|```
   181|
   182|## Component Design
   183|
   184|### Anatomy of a Well-Designed Component
   185|
   186|Every UI component should have clear states, consistent spacing, and predictable behavior:
   187|
   188|| State | Visual Treatment | Example |
   189||---|---|---|
   190|| **Default** | Base styling | Button at rest |
   191|| **Hover** | Subtle shift — background, shadow, or scale | `background` lightens 5-10% |
   192|| **Active / Pressed** | Compressed feel — reduced shadow, slight inset | `transform: scale(0.98)` |
   193|| **Focus** | High-visibility ring, no outline removal | `:focus-visible` ring |
   194|| **Disabled** | Reduced opacity, `cursor: not-allowed` | `opacity: 0.5` |
   195|| **Loading** | Spinner or skeleton, disabled interaction | Inline spinner replacing label |
   196|
   197|### Design Token Architecture
   198|
   199|Structure tokens in three layers for maintainability:
   200|
   201|```css
   202|/* Layer 1: Primitive values */
   203|--blue-500: oklch(0.55 0.2 250);
   204|--gray-100: oklch(0.95 0.005 250);
   205|--radius-md: 0.5rem;
   206|
   207|/* Layer 2: Semantic aliases */
   208|--color-primary: var(--blue-500);
   209|--color-surface: var(--gray-100);
   210|--radius-button: var(--radius-md);
   211|
   212|/* Layer 3: Component-specific */
   213|--btn-bg: var(--color-primary);
   214|--btn-radius: var(--radius-button);
   215|--btn-padding: var(--space-2) var(--space-4);
   216|```
   217|
   218|This three-layer approach allows theme switching by remapping Layer 2 without touching components.
   219|
   220|## Interaction Patterns
   221|
   222|### Motion and Animation
   223|
   224|Use motion to communicate state changes, not to decorate. Focus on high-impact moments:
   225|
   226|| Interaction | Duration | Easing | Purpose |
   227||---|---|---|---|
   228|| Button hover | 150ms | `ease-out` | Acknowledge interaction |
   229|| Modal open | 250ms | `ease-out` | Draw attention |
   230|| Modal close | 200ms | `ease-in` | Quick dismissal |
   231|| Page transition | 300ms | `ease-in-out` | Maintain spatial context |
   232|| Stagger reveal | 50–80ms delay per item | `ease-out` | Sequential content loading |
   233|| Micro-feedback | 100ms | `ease-out` | Toggle, checkbox, switch |
   234|
   235|```css
   236|/* Staggered entrance animation */
   237|.stagger-item {
   238|  opacity: 0;
   239|  translate: 0 1rem;
   240|  animation: reveal 0.5s ease-out forwards;
   241|}
   242|.stagger-item:nth-child(1) { animation-delay: 0ms; }
   243|.stagger-item:nth-child(2) { animation-delay: 60ms; }
   244|.stagger-item:nth-child(3) { animation-delay: 120ms; }
   245|
   246|@keyframes reveal {
   247|  to { opacity: 1; translate: 0 0; }
   248|}
   249|```
   250|
   251|### Scroll-Driven Effects
   252|
   253|Use native `animation-timeline: scroll()` (behind `@supports`) for parallax and reveal effects without JavaScript. Wrap in feature detection to gracefully degrade.
   254|
   255|## Design Quality Checklist
   256|
   257|Before shipping, verify against these criteria:
   258|
   259|- [ ] **Typography**: Intentional font pairing, consistent scale, readable line lengths
   260|- [ ] **Color**: Cohesive palette, WCAG contrast met, semantic feedback colors defined
   261|- [ ] **Spacing**: Consistent rhythm using spacing tokens, no ad-hoc pixel values
   262|- [ ] **Hierarchy**: Clear visual flow — eye path follows intended reading order
   263|- [ ] **Responsiveness**: Tested at mobile, tablet, desktop; no horizontal overflow
   264|- [ ] **Accessibility**: Keyboard navigable, focus visible, screen-reader tested, motion-safe
   265|- [ ] **States**: All interactive elements have hover, active, focus, disabled, and loading states
   266|- [ ] **Personality**: Design has a clear point-of-view — not generic template aesthetic
   267|- [ ] **Performance**: Images optimized, fonts subset, animations GPU-accelerated (`transform`, `opacity`)
   268|- [ ] **Dark mode**: If supported, surfaces use layered lightness, not inverted colors

{"content": "     1|# UI/UX Design
     2|
     3|**Name:** ui-ux-design  
     4|**Description:** Modern UI/UX design principles, patterns, and best practices for web and mobile applications. Use when building user interfaces, designing layouts, choosing color palettes, implementing responsive design, ensuring accessibility (WCAG), or creating beautiful modern applications. Includes 2026 design trends, Tailwind CSS patterns, Shadcn/ui integration, micro-interactions, and mobile-first responsive design.
     5|
     6|---
     7|
     8|## When to Use This Skill
     9|
    10|Activate this skill when:
    11|- Building or designing web/mobile interfaces
    12|- Choosing colors, typography, or layout systems
    13|- Implementing responsive design (mobile-first)
    14|- Ensuring accessibility compliance (WCAG 2.2)
    15|- Setting up Shadcn/ui + Tailwind CSS projects
    16|- Creating micro-interactions and animations
    17|- Reviewing UI/UX decisions before coding
    18|
    19|---
    20|
    21|## Core Design Principles
    22|
    23|### 1. Mobile-First Always
    24|- Start with 320px width (smallest phone)
    25|- Breakpoints: 576px (phone), 768px (tablet), 992px (laptop), 1200px (desktop)
    26|- Single-column default, expand only when space allows
    27|
    28|### 2. Visual Hierarchy
    29|Guide user attention using:
    30|- **Size:** Larger = more important
    31|- **Color:** Bright/contrasting = attention
    32|- **Whitespace:** More space = emphasis
    33|- **Proximity:** Related items grouped together
    34|- **Contrast:** Dark on light or light on dark (4.5:1 minimum for text)
    35|
    36|### 3. Whitespace is Your Weapon
    37|- Space elements in multiples of 8px (8, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64)
    38|- Breathing room between sections: 48-64px minimum
    39|- Padding inside cards: 24-32px
    40|
    41|---
    42|
    43|## Quick Reference
    44|
    45|### Color System
    46|Build a primary color scale (50-900):
    47|- **Primary:** Brand color (CTAs, links, active states)
    48|- **Neutrals:** Grays 50-900 (text, backgrounds, borders)
    49|- **Semantic:** Success (green), Error (red), Warning (yellow/orange)
    50|
    51|Tools: Huevy.app, Coolors.co, Adobe Color
    52|
    53|### Typography Scale (8px baseline)
    54|```
    55|text-xs:   12px / 16px line-height
    56|text-sm:   14px / 20px
    57|text-base: 16px / 24px (body default)
    58|text-lg:   18px / 28px
    59|text-xl:   20px / 28px
    60|text-2xl:  24px / 32px
    61|text-3xl:  30px / 36px (section headers)
    62|text-4xl:  36px / 40px
    63|text-5xl:  48px / 1 (hero titles)
    64|```
    65|
    66|**Font pairing:** 2 fonts max (sans-serif for UI, optional serif for headings)
    67|
    68|### Layout Patterns
    69|- **CSS Grid:** 2D layouts (page structure)
    70|- **Flexbox:** 1D layouts (component internals)
    71|- **Auto-fit grid:** `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(280px, 1fr))` (no media queries!)
    72|
    73|### Micro-Interactions
    74|- **Hover:** Scale 1.05x (buttons feel clickable)
    75|- **Click:** Scale 0.95x (tactile feedback)
    76|- **Duration:** 0.2-0.3s max (keep it subtle)
    77|- **Animate only:** `transform` and `opacity` (GPU accelerated)
    78|
    79|### Accessibility (WCAG 2.2)
    80|- **Text contrast:** 4.5:1 minimum (normal text), 3:1 (large text)
    81|- **UI components:** 3:1 contrast minimum
    82|- **Keyboard navigation:** Tab order logical, focus states visible (3:1 contrast)
    83|- **ARIA labels:** Always provide for buttons, images, interactive elements
    84|
    85|---
    86|
    87|## Shadcn/ui + Tailwind Stack
    88|
    89|### Setup (Next.js)
    90|```bash
    91|npx create-next-app@latest project-name --typescript --tailwind --app
    92|cd project-name
    93|npx shadcn@latest init
    94|```
    95|
    96|Choose: Style (Default), Base color (Blue or custom), CSS variables (Yes)
    97|
    98|### Adding Components
    99|```bash
   100|npx shadcn@latest add button
   101|npx shadcn@latest add card
   102|npx shadcn@latest add dialog
   103|npx shadcn@latest add calendar
   104|```
   105|
   106|Components appear in `components/ui/` — you own the code, customize freely.
   107|
   108|### Tailwind Best Practices
   109|- Use design tokens (not arbitrary values): `p-4` not `p-[17px]`
   110|- Responsive utilities: `w-full md:w-1/2 lg:w-1/3`
   111|- Dark mode: `dark:bg-gray-900 dark:text-white`
   112|
   113|---
   114|
   115|## Pre-Build Checklist
   116|
   117|Before writing code, confirm:
   118|- [ ] Color palette defined (primary + neutrals + semantic colors)
   119|- [ ] Typography scale chosen (6-8 sizes)
   120|- [ ] Component library picked (Shadcn + Tailwind)
   121|- [ ] Mobile breakpoints planned (576px, 768px, 992px)
   122|- [ ] Accessibility contrast ratios checked (4.5:1 text, 3:1 UI)
   123|- [ ] Micro-interaction list (hover, click, success states)
   124|- [ ] Grid layout sketched (mobile → desktop progression)
   125|
   126|---
   127|
   128|## Inspiration Sources
   129|
   130|**Study these products:**
   131|- Linear (linear.app) — Best keyboard-first UI, subtle animations
   132|- Stripe Dashboard — Clean data visualization, perfect spacing
   133|- Vercel — Minimalist, fast, modern gradients
   134|- Notion — Intuitive drag-and-drop, clear hierarchy
   135|
   136|**Tools:**
   137|- Figma (mockups before coding)
   138|- WebAIM Contrast Checker (accessibility)
   139|- Coolors/Huevy (color palettes)
   140|
   141|---
   142|
   143|## The 5 Laws of Beautiful UI
   144|
   145|1. **Contrast creates hierarchy** (big vs small, dark vs light)
   146|2. **Whitespace creates calm** (never fear empty space)
   147|3. **Consistency builds trust** (same patterns repeated)
   148|4. **Feedback confirms action** (animations, success messages)
   149|5. **Accessibility includes everyone** (contrast, keyboard, screen readers)
   150|
   151|---
   152|
   153|## Full Reference
   154|
   155|For comprehensive deep-dives (component patterns, animation examples, responsive grid techniques), see `UI_UX_MASTER_GUIDE.md` in this skill directory.

   161|---
   162|
   163|# AGENT DIRECTIVE: Execution Protocol
   164|
   165|> **CRITICAL INSTRUCTION FOR ALL MIFECO AGENTS**
   166|
   167|## The Golden Rule
   168|
   169|**DO NOT SUGGEST ACTIONS. EXECUTE THEM.**
   170|
   171|### What This Means
   172|
   173|| ❌ DON'T | ✅ DO |
   174||---------|-------|
   175|| "You could create a file..." | Create the file. |
   176|| "I recommend running this command..." | Run the command. |
   177|| "Here's a script you might use..." | Execute the script. |
   178|| "Would you like me to...?" | Just do it and report results. |
   179|
   180|### Execution Standard
   181|
   182|When assigned a task:
   183|
   184|1. **Execute immediately** - Don't ask for permission unless explicitly blocked
   185|2. **Report what you did** - Not what you "would" do
   186|3. **Show results** - Output, files created, changes made
   187|4. **Escalate on failure** - Don't stall, notify immediately
   188|
   189|## Failure Protocol
   190|
   191|If you **CANNOT** perform an action:
   192|
   193|**STEP 1:** Try alternative approaches (max 2 attempts)
   194|
   195|**STEP 2:** If still blocked, send immediate notification:
   196|
   197|```json
   198|{
   199|  "timestamp": "ISO-8601",
   200|  "task_id": "original-task-id",
   201|  "from": "your-agent-id",
   202|  "to": "ceo",
   203|  "type": "alert",
   204|  "priority": "high",
   205|  "task": "FAILED: [brief description]",
   206|  "payload": {
   207|    "error": "Specific error message",
   208|    "attempted": ["what you tried"],
   209|    "blocker": "why it failed",
   210|    "needs": "what is needed to proceed"
   211|  },
   212|  "status": "failed"
   213|}
   214|```
   215|
   216|**STEP 3:** Send Telegram notification:
   217|
   218|```
   219|🚨 AGENT FAILURE ALERT
   220|
   221|Agent: [your-agent-id]
   222|Task: [task_id]
   223|Error: [specific error]
   224|
   225|Needs: [what is required]
   226|Timestamp: [ISO-8601]
   227|```
   228|
   229|## Telegram Notification Template
   230|
   231|Use this exact format for Telegram alerts:
   232|
   233|```
   234|🚨 [AGENT] FAILED: [Brief Task Description]
   235|
   236|Error: [Specific error message]
   237|Attempted: [What you tried]
   238|Blocker: [Why it failed]
   239|
   240|Needs CEO/Board attention to proceed.
   241|Task ID: [task_id]
   242|```
   243|
   244|## When to Notify
   245|
   246|Send Telegram alert immediately for:
   247|- ❌ Tool execution failures (exec, edit, write fail)
   248|- ❌ Permission denied errors
   249|- ❌ External API failures (non-recoverable)
   250|- ❌ Missing required files/data
   251|- ❌ Agent spawn failures
   252|- ❌ Security/policy blocks
   253|
   254|**DO NOT** alert for:
   255|- ✅ Retrying after transient failures (network, rate limits)
   256|- ✅ Clarifying ambiguous instructions (ask first)
   257|- ✅ Expected delays (report in status updates)
   258|
   259|## Examples
   260|
   261|### Good Execution
   262|
   263|User: "Create a backup script"
   264|
   265|Agent:
   266|```
   267|Created backup.sh in /home/bob/scripts/
   268|
   269|Contents:
   270|#!/bin/bash
   271|# Backup script
   272|tar -czf backup-$(date +%Y%m%d).tar.gz ~/workspace
   273|
   274|Tested: ✅ Executes successfully

   276|```
   277|

   289|```
   290|

   293|All agent responses must follow this structure:
   294|
   295|```
   296|[EXECUTION RESULT]
   297|
   298|What was done: [specific actions]

   301|Status: ✅ Complete | ⏳ In Progress | ❌ Blocked
   302|
   303|If Blocked:

     3|description: >
     4|  Web access priority configuration for OpenClaw agents.
     5|  Primary: searXNG for web search.
     6|  Fallback 1: DuckDuckGo (browser navigation + web_fetch).

     8|---
     9|
    10|# Web Access Priority Stack
    11|
    12|## Priority Order
    13|
    14|```
    15|1. searXNG (PRIMARY)
    16|   └── Use for: General web search, news, current events, broad search queries
    17|   └── Method: use the configured searXNG instance first
    18|   
    19|2. DuckDuckGo (FALLBACK 1)
    20|   └── Use for: When searXNG is unavailable or incomplete
    21|   └── Method: browser navigation to duckduckgo.com + web_fetch
    22|   
    23|3. Brave Search API (FALLBACK 2)
    24|   └── Use for: Last resort only
    25|   └── Tool: web_search
    26|```
    27|
    28|## When to Use Each
    29|
    30|### agent-browser (Primary)
    31|Use when:
    32|- Filling out forms
    33|- Taking screenshots of pages
    34|- Extracting data from dynamic websites
    35|- Testing web applications
    36|- Logging into sites
    37|- Clicking buttons/navigation
    38|- Need JavaScript-rendered content
    39|
    40|Example:
    41|```bash
    42|agent-browser open https://example.com/login
    43|agent-browser snapshot -i
    44|agent-browser fill @e1 "username"
    45|agent-browser fill @e2 "password"
    46|agent-browser click @e3
    47|```
    48|
    49|### Brave Search (Fallback 1)
    50|Use when:
    51|- Quick information lookup
    52|- News search
    53|- General queries
    54|- No need to interact with page
    55|
    56|Example:
    57|```python
    58|web_search(query="latest AI trends 2026", count=5)
    59|```
    60|
    61|### DuckDuckGo (Fallback 2)
    62|Use when:
    63|- Brave API rate limited
    64|- Anonymous search needed
    65|- Both agent-browser and Brave unavailable
    66|
    67|Example:
    68|```bash
    69|# Navigate to DuckDuckGo
    70|agent-browser open "https://duckduckgo.com/?q=your+query"
    71|agent-browser snapshot
    72|# Or use web_fetch on results page
    73|```
    74|
    75|## Configuration
    76|
    77|Set environment variables for priority enforcement:
    78|
    79|```bash
    80|# Primary web tool
    81|export OPENCLAW_WEB_PRIMARY="agent-browser"
    82|
    83|# Fallback chain
    84|export OPENCLAW_WEB_FALLBACK_1="brave"
    85|export OPENCLAW_WEB_FALLBACK_2="duckduckgo"
    86|
    87|# Agent-browser specific settings
    88|export AGENT_BROWSER_HEADED=0        # Headless mode
    89|export AGENT_BROWSER_CONTENT_BOUNDARIES=1  # Wrap output for safety
    90|export AGENT_BROWSER_MAX_OUTPUT=50000 # Limit output size
    91|```
    92|
    93|## Usage in Agents
    94|
    95|When an agent needs web access, it should:
    96|
    97|1. **Try agent-browser first** for any interactive or complex task
    98|2. **Fall back to web_search** for simple queries if agent-browser fails
    99|3. **Use DuckDuckGo** as last resort if both fail
   100|
   101|### Helper Function Pattern
   102|
   103|```bash
   104|# Function to try web access in priority order
   105|web_access() {
   106|    local url="$1"
   107|    local mode="${2:-snapshot}"  # snapshot, screenshot, or interactive
   108|    
   109|    # Try agent-browser first
   110|    if command -v agent-browser &> /dev/null; then
   111|        echo "Using agent-browser..."
   112|        agent-browser open "$url"
   113|        if [ "$mode" = "snapshot" ]; then
   114|            agent-browser snapshot -i
   115|        elif [ "$mode" = "screenshot" ]; then
   116|            agent-browser screenshot
   117|        fi
   118|        return 0
   119|    fi
   120|    
   121|    # Fallback to web_fetch for static content
   122|    echo "Agent-browser not available, trying web_fetch..."
   123|    web_fetch "$url"
   124|    return $?
   125|}
   126|```
   127|
   128|## Error Handling
   129|
   130|If agent-browser fails:
   131|1. Log the error
   132|2. Automatically try web_search for the same query
   133|3. If web_search fails (rate limit), use DuckDuckGo
   134|4. Report which tool succeeded
   135|
   136|## Rate Limit Awareness
   137|
   138|| Tool | Rate Limit | Backup Strategy |
   139||------|------------|-----------------|
   140|| agent-browser | None (local browser) | N/A |
   141|| Brave Search | 5/hour (free tier) | Switch to DuckDuckGo |
   142|| DuckDuckGo | None | N/A |
   143|
   144|## Integration with Existing Tools
   145|
   146|This priority stack integrates with OpenClaw's existing tools:
   147|- `browser` tool (OpenClaw native) - Use for simple navigation
   148|- `web_search` tool (Brave API) - Use for quick searches  
   149|- `web_fetch` tool - Use for static content extraction
   150|- `agent-browser` (Vercel Labs) - Use for complex automation
   151|
   152|## Testing
   153|
   154|Verify the stack works:
   155|
   156|```bash
   157|# Test agent-browser
   158|agent-browser open https://example.com && agent-browser snapshot -i
   159|
   160|# Test web_search
   161|web_search query="test search"
   162|
   163|# Test DuckDuckGo fallback
   164|agent-browser open "https://duckduckgo.com/?q=test+query"
   165|```
   166|

   169|- agent-browser requires Chromium/Chrome installed

{"content": "     1|---
     2|name: linkedin
     3|description: LinkedIn automation via browser relay or cookies for messaging, profile viewing, and network actions.
     4|homepage: https://linkedin.com
     5|metadata: {"clawdbot":{"emoji":"💼"}}
     6|---
     7|
     8|# LinkedIn
     9|
    10|Use browser automation to interact with LinkedIn - check messages, view profiles, search, and send connection requests.
    11|
    12|## Connection Methods
    13|
    14|### Option 1: Chrome Extension Relay (Recommended)
    15|1. Open LinkedIn in Chrome and log in
    16|2. Click the Clawdbot Browser Relay toolbar icon to attach the tab
    17|3. Use `browser` tool with `profile="chrome"`
    18|
    19|### Option 2: Isolated Browser
    20|1. Use `browser` tool with `profile="clawd"` 
    21|2. Navigate to linkedin.com
    22|3. Log in manually (one-time setup)
    23|4. Session persists for future use
    24|
    25|## Common Operations
    26|
    27|### Check Connection Status
    28|```
    29|browser action=snapshot profile=chrome targetUrl="https://www.linkedin.com/feed/"
    30|```
    31|
    32|### View Notifications/Messages
    33|```
    34|browser action=navigate profile=chrome targetUrl="https://www.linkedin.com/messaging/"
    35|browser action=snapshot profile=chrome
    36|```
    37|
    38|### Search People
    39|```
    40|browser action=navigate profile=chrome targetUrl="https://www.linkedin.com/search/results/people/?keywords=QUERY"
    41|browser action=snapshot profile=chrome
    42|```
    43|
    44|### View Profile
    45|```
    46|browser action=navigate profile=chrome targetUrl="https://www.linkedin.com/in/USERNAME/"
    47|browser action=snapshot profile=chrome
    48|```
    49|
    50|### Send Message (confirm with user first!)
    51|1. Navigate to messaging or profile
    52|2. Use `browser action=act` with click/type actions
    53|3. Always confirm message content before sending
    54|
    55|## Safety Rules
    56|- **Never send messages without explicit user approval**
    57|- **Never accept/send connection requests without confirmation**
    58|- **Avoid rapid automated actions** - LinkedIn is aggressive about detecting automation
    59|- Rate limit: ~30 actions per hour max recommended
    60|
    61|## Session Cookie Method (Advanced)
    62|If browser relay isn't available, extract the `li_at` cookie from browser:
    63|1. Open LinkedIn in browser, log in
    64|2. DevTools → Application → Cookies → linkedin.com
    65|3. Copy `li_at` value
    66|4. Store securely for API requests
    67|
    68|## Troubleshooting
    69|- If logged out: Re-authenticate in browser
    70|- If rate limited: Wait 24 hours, reduce action frequency
    71|- If CAPTCHA: Complete manually in browser, then resume
    72|
    73|---
    74|
    75|# AGENT DIRECTIVE: Execution Protocol
    76|
    77|> **CRITICAL INSTRUCTION FOR ALL MIFECO AGENTS**
    78|
    79|## The Golden Rule
    80|
    81|**DO NOT SUGGEST ACTIONS. EXECUTE THEM.**
    82|
    83|### What This Means
    84|
    85|| ❌ DON'T | ✅ DO |
    86||---------|-------|
    87|| "You could create a file..." | Create the file. |
    88|| "I recommend running this command..." | Run the command. |
    89|| "Here's a script you might use..." | Execute the script. |
    90|| "Would you like me to...?" | Just do it and report results. |
    91|
    92|### Execution Standard
    93|
    94|When assigned a task:
    95|
    96|1. **Execute immediately** - Don't ask for permission unless explicitly blocked
    97|2. **Report what you did** - Not what you "would" do
    98|3. **Show results** - Output, files created, changes made
    99|4. **Escalate on failure** - Don't stall, notify immediately
   100|
   101|## Failure Protocol
   102|
   103|If you **CANNOT** perform an action:
   104|
   105|**STEP 1:** Try alternative approaches (max 2 attempts)
   106|
   107|**STEP 2:** If still blocked, send immediate notification:
   108|
   109|```json
   110|{
   111|  "timestamp": "ISO-8601",
   112|  "task_id": "original-task-id",
   113|  "from": "your-agent-id",
   114|  "to": "ceo",
   115|  "type": "alert",
   116|  "priority": "high",
   117|  "task": "FAILED: [brief description]",
   118|  "payload": {
   119|    "error": "Specific error message",
   120|    "attempted": ["what you tried"],
   121|    "blocker": "why it failed",
   122|    "needs": "what is needed to proceed"
   123|  },
   124|  "status": "failed"
   125|}
   126|```
   127|
   128|**STEP 3:** Send Telegram notification:
   129|
   130|```
   131|🚨 AGENT FAILURE ALERT
   132|
   133|Agent: [your-agent-id]
   134|Task: [task_id]
   135|Error: [specific error]
   136|
   137|Needs: [what is required]
   138|Timestamp: [ISO-8601]
   139|```
   140|
   141|## Telegram Notification Template
   142|
   143|Use this exact format for Telegram alerts:
   144|
   145|```
   146|🚨 [AGENT] FAILED: [Brief Task Description]
   147|
   148|Error: [Specific error message]
   149|Attempted: [What you tried]
   150|Blocker: [Why it failed]
   151|
   152|Needs CEO/Board attention to proceed.
   153|Task ID: [task_id]
   154|```
   155|
   156|## When to Notify
   157|
   158|Send Telegram alert immediately for:
   159|- ❌ Tool execution failures (exec, edit, write fail)
   160|- ❌ Permission denied errors
   161|- ❌ External API failures (non-recoverable)
   162|- ❌ Missing required files/data
   163|- ❌ Agent spawn failures
   164|- ❌ Security/policy blocks
   165|
   166|**DO NOT** alert for:
   167|- ✅ Retrying after transient failures (network, rate limits)
   168|- ✅ Clarifying ambiguous instructions (ask first)
   169|- ✅ Expected delays (report in status updates)
   170|
   171|## Examples
   172|
   173|### Good Execution
   174|
   175|User: "Create a backup script"
   176|
   177|Agent:
   178|```
   179|Created backup.sh in /home/bob/scripts/
   180|
   181|Contents:
   182|#!/bin/bash
   183|# Backup script
   184|tar -czf backup-$(date +%Y%m%d).tar.gz ~/workspace
   185|
   186|Tested: ✅ Executes successfully
   187|Next backup: Tonight at 2 AM via cron
   188|```
   189|
   190|### Good Failure Handling
   191|
   192|Agent encounters error:
   193|```
   194|Attempt 1: Failed - Permission denied on /etc/config
   195|Attempt 2: Failed - sudo not available in this environment
   196|
   197|🚨 Sending alert to CEO...
   198|
   199|Telegram notification sent.
   200|Waiting for escalation.
   201|```
   202|
   203|## Mandatory Footer
   204|
   205|All agent responses must follow this structure:
   206|
   207|```
   208|[EXECUTION RESULT]
   209|
   210|What was done: [specific actions]
   211|Output/Results: [what happened]
   212|Files changed: [list if any]
   213|Status: ✅ Complete | ⏳ In Progress | ❌ Blocked
   214|
   215|If Blocked:
   216|🚨 Telegram alert sent: [yes/no]
   217|Next action: [what happens next]
   218|```
   219|
   220|## Agent Self-Check
   221|
   222|Before responding, verify:
   223|
   224|- [ ] Did I actually DO the thing, or just describe it?
   225|- [ ] Did I run the command, or just paste it?
   226|- [ ] Did I create the file, or just show the content?
   227|- [ ] If blocked, did I send the Telegram alert?
   228|
   229|**Remember: Actions speak louder than suggestions.**
   230|---
   231|
   232|## AUTO-CONTINUE SYSTEM
   233|
   234|This agent is monitored by the auto-continue system. If your response contains:
   235|- Suggestions without actions ('could', 'would', 'might')
   236|- Passive language ('consider', 'think about')
   237|- Questions instead of execution
   238|
   239|The system will automatically generate a CONTINUE prompt within 10 minutes.
   240|To prevent this: ALWAYS execute immediately and show concrete results.
   241|
   242|See AGENT_DIRECTIVE.md for complete protocol.

    43|- **No hashtags in the body.** If you must, 3-5 at the very bottom.
    44|- **No emojis as bullet points.** One emoji per post max, if any.
    45|- **First line is everything.** It shows in the preview before "...see more"
    46|- **End with a question.** Drives comments, which drives reach.
    47|- **Under 1300 characters** for optimal engagement. Can go longer for story posts.
    48|

    53|- No humble brags disguised as lessons
    54|- No "I'm excited to share..." — just share it
    55|- Specific > generic. "We grew from 12 to 47 customers" beats "We experienced significant growth"

   117|Blocker: [Why it failed]
   118|
   119|Needs CEO/Board attention to proceed.
   120|Task ID: [task_id]
   121|```
   122|
   123|## When to Notify
   124|
   125|Send Telegram alert immediately for:
   126|- ❌ Tool execution failures (exec, edit, write fail)
   127|- ❌ Permission denied errors
   128|- ❌ External API failures (non-recoverable)
   129|- ❌ Missing required files/data
   130|- ❌ Agent spawn failures
   131|- ❌ Security/policy blocks
   132|
   133|**DO NOT** alert for:
   134|- ✅ Retrying after transient failures (network, rate limits)
   135|- ✅ Clarifying ambiguous instructions (ask first)
   136|- ✅ Expected delays (report in status updates)
   137|
   138|## Examples
   139|
   140|### Good Execution
   141|
   142|User: "Create a backup script"
   143|
   144|Agent:
   145|```
   146|Created backup.sh in /home/bob/scripts/
   147|
   148|Contents:
   149|#!/bin/bash
   150|# Backup script
   151|tar -czf backup-$(date +%Y%m%d).tar.gz ~/workspace
   152|
   153|Tested: ✅ Executes successfully
   154|Next backup: Tonight at 2 AM via cron
   155|```
   156|
   157|### Good Failure Handling
   158|
   159|Agent encounters error:
   160|```
   161|Attempt 1: Failed - Permission denied on /etc/config
   162|Attempt 2: Failed - sudo not available in this environment
   163|

   165|

   167|Waiting for escalation.
   168|```
   169|
   170|## Mandatory Footer
   171|
   172|All agent responses must follow this structure:
   173|
   174|```
   175|[EXECUTION RESULT]
   176|
   177|What was done: [specific actions]
   178|Output/Results: [what happened]
   179|Files changed: [list if any]
   180|Status: ✅ Complete | ⏳ In Progress | ❌ Blocked
   181|
   182|If Blocked:
   183|🚨 Telegram alert sent: [yes/no]
   184|Next action: [what happens next]
   185|```
   186|
   187|## Agent Self-Check
   188|
   189|Before responding, verify:
   190|
   191|- [ ] Did I actually DO the thing, or just describe it?
   192|- [ ] Did I run the command, or just paste it?
   193|- [ ] Did I create the file, or just show the content?
   194|- [ ] If blocked, did I send the Telegram alert?
   195|
   196|**Remember: Actions speak louder than suggestions.**
   197|---
   198|
   199|## AUTO-CONTINUE SYSTEM

   201|This agent is monitored by the auto-continue system. If your response contains:
   202|- Suggestions without actions ('could', 'would', 'might')

{"content": "     1|---
     2|name: marketing
     3|version: 1.0.0
     4|description: "Social media automation, content scheduling, analytics tracking, and campaign management. Transform your AI agent into a marketing powerhouse that handles multi-platform content strategy."
     5|author: openclaw
     6|---
     7|
     8|# Marketing Skill 📢
     9|
    10|**Turn your AI agent into a strategic marketing partner.**
    11|
    12|Handle social media, content scheduling, analytics, and campaign management across platforms — without constant manual input.
    13|
    14|---
    15|
    16|## What This Skill Does
    17|
    18|✅ **Content Creation** — Generate posts, threads, newsletters, and visual content descriptions
    19|✅ **Multi-Platform Management** — Twitter/X, LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, newsletters
    20|✅ **Scheduling & Automation** — Plan content calendars, schedule posts, maintain consistency
    21|✅ **Analytics Tracking** — Monitor engagement, track KPIs, identify trends
    22|✅ **Campaign Management** — Plan campaigns, track performance, A/B testing insights
    23|✅ **Brand Voice Consistency** — Maintain tone and style across all content
    24|
    25|---
    26|
    27|## Quick Start
    28|
    29|1. Configure your marketing preferences in `TOOLS.md`:
    30|```markdown
    31|### Marketing
    32|- Brand voice: [Professional/Casual/Witty/etc.]
    33|- Primary platforms: [Twitter, LinkedIn, etc.]
    34|- Posting frequency: [Daily/3x week/etc.]
    35|- Target audience: [Description]
    36|```
    37|
    38|2. Set up your content calendar:
    39|```bash
    40|./scripts/content-calendar.sh init
    41|```
    42|
    43|3. Start creating content!
    44|
    45|---
    46|
    47|## Content Strategy Framework
    48|
    49|### The AIDA Model for Posts
    50|
    51|| Stage | Purpose | Example Hook |
    52||-------|---------|--------------|
    53|| **Attention** | Stop the scroll | "Most marketers waste 80% of their budget on this..." |
    54|| **Interest** | Build curiosity | "Here's what the top 1% do differently..." |
    55|| **Desire** | Create want | "Imagine doubling your engagement in 30 days..." |
    56|| **Action** | Drive behavior | "Try this today: [actionable tip]" |
    57|
    58|### Platform-Specific Best Practices
    59|
    60|**Twitter/X:**
    61|- Optimal length: 100-280 characters
    62|- Use threads for long-form (5-15 tweets)
    63|- Hook in first line — no fluff
    64|- 1-2 hashtags max
    65|- Best times: 9am, 12pm, 5pm local
    66|
    67|**LinkedIn:**
    68|- Professional but personable tone
    69|- Open with a bold statement or question
    70|- Use line breaks for readability
    71|- 1300-2000 characters performs best
    72|- Include relevant hashtags (3-5)
    73|
    74|**Instagram:**
    75|- Visual-first thinking
    76|- Captions: tell a story
    77|- Hashtag strategy: 20-30 in first comment
    78|- Call-to-action in every post
    79|- Carousel posts get highest engagement
    80|
    81|**Newsletter:**
    82|- Subject lines: 40-60 characters
    83|- Preview text matters (first 90 chars)
    84|- One clear CTA per email
    85|- Personal stories increase open rates
    86|- Send consistently (same day/time)
    87|
    88|---
    89|
    90|## Content Calendar Management
    91|
    92|### Monthly Planning Template
    93|
    94|```markdown
    95|# [Month] Content Calendar
    96|
    97|## Themes
    98|- Week 1: [Theme]
    99|- Week 2: [Theme]
   100|- Week 3: [Theme]
   101|- Week 4: [Theme]
   102|
   103|## Key Dates
   104|- [Date]: [Event/Holiday]
   105|
   106|## Content Mix (per week)
   107|- Educational: 3
   108|- Promotional: 1
   109|- Engagement: 2
   110|- User-generated/Curated: 1
   111|
   112|## Platform Schedule
   113|| Day | Twitter | LinkedIn | Instagram | Newsletter |
   114||-----|---------|----------|-----------|------------|
   115|| Mon | Thread  | Article  | Carousel  | -          |
   116|| Tue | Tips    | -        | Story     | -          |
   117|| Wed | Poll    | Post     | Reel      | Send       |
   118|| Thu | Thread  | -        | Story     | -          |
   119|| Fri | Fun     | Post     | Post      | -          |
   120|```
   121|
   122|### Content Batching Workflow
   123|
   124|1. **Ideation Day** (Monthly) — Brainstorm 30+ content ideas
   125|2. **Creation Day** (Weekly) — Write next week's content in one session
   126|3. **Scheduling Day** (Weekly) — Load content into scheduler
   127|4. **Engagement Day** (Daily) — Respond to comments, engage with community
   128|
   129|---
   130|
   131|## Analytics & KPIs
   132|
   133|### Key Metrics to Track
   134|
   135|| Metric | What It Tells You | Target Growth |
   136||--------|-------------------|---------------|
   137|| Impressions | Reach | +10% monthly |
   138|| Engagement Rate | Content quality | >3% (Twitter), >5% (LinkedIn) |
   139|| Click-through Rate | CTA effectiveness | >2% |
   140|| Follower Growth | Audience building | +5% monthly |
   141|| Conversion Rate | Business impact | Varies by goal |
   142|
   143|### Weekly Analytics Template
   144|
   145|```markdown
   146|# Week of [Date] - Analytics Report
   147|
   148|## Summary
   149|- Total impressions: [X]
   150|- Total engagement: [X]
   151|- New followers: [X]
   152|- Top performing post: [Link]
   153|
   154|## Platform Breakdown
   155|
   156|### Twitter
   157|- Impressions: [X]
   158|- Engagement rate: [X]%
   159|- Best day: [Day]
   160|- Top tweet: [Content]
   161|
   162|### LinkedIn
   163|- Impressions: [X]
   164|- Engagement rate: [X]%
   165|- Comments: [X]
   166|- Top post: [Content]
   167|
   168|## Insights
   169|- What worked: [Analysis]
   170|- What didn't: [Analysis]
   171|- Next week focus: [Adjustment]
   172|```
   173|
   174|---
   175|
   176|## Campaign Management
   177|
   178|### Campaign Planning Template
   179|
   180|```markdown
   181|# Campaign: [Name]
   182|
   183|## Overview
   184|- **Goal:** [Specific, measurable goal]
   185|- **Timeline:** [Start] - [End]
   186|- **Budget:** [Amount if applicable]
   187|- **Success Metrics:** [KPIs]
   188|
   189|## Target Audience
   190|- Demographics: [Age, location, etc.]
   191|- Pain points: [Problems we solve]
   192|- Platforms: [Where they hang out]
   193|
   194|## Content Assets
   195|- [ ] Main announcement post
   196|- [ ] Supporting content (X posts)
   197|- [ ] Visuals/graphics
   198|- [ ] Landing page copy
   199|- [ ] Email sequence
   200|
   201|## Schedule
   202|| Date | Platform | Content | CTA |
   203||------|----------|---------|-----|
   204|| [Date] | Twitter | [Content] | [Action] |
   205|
   206|## Results (fill after)
   207|- Reach: [X]
   208|- Engagement: [X]
   209|- Conversions: [X]
   210|- ROI: [X]
   211|- Learnings: [What we learned]
   212|```
   213|
   214|---
   215|
   216|## Content Generation Prompts
   217|
   218|### For Twitter Threads
   219|```
   220|Create a Twitter thread on [TOPIC]:
   221|- Hook that stops scrolling
   222|- 5-10 tweets of value
   223|- Each tweet stands alone but builds on previous
   224|- End with CTA and recap
   225|- Conversational but authoritative tone
   226|```
   227|
   228|### For LinkedIn Posts
   229|```
   230|Write a LinkedIn post about [TOPIC]:
   231|- Opening hook (1-2 lines)
   232|- Personal story or observation
   233|- Key insight or lesson
   234|- Actionable takeaway
   235|- Engagement question
   236|- 1200-1500 characters
   237|```
   238|
   239|### For Newsletter
   240|```
   241|Draft newsletter on [TOPIC]:
   242|- Compelling subject line (3 options)
   243|- Personal opening
   244|- Main value content
   245|- One clear CTA
   246|- PS line for bonus engagement
   247|```
   248|
   249|---
   250|
   251|## Automation Workflows
   252|
   253|### Daily Marketing Routine
   254|
   255|```markdown
   256|## Morning (30 min)
   257|- [ ] Check overnight engagement
   258|- [ ] Respond to comments/DMs
   259|- [ ] Share 2-3 relevant posts from others
   260|- [ ] Check trending topics for opportunities
   261|
   262|## Afternoon (15 min)
   263|- [ ] Post scheduled content (if not automated)
   264|- [ ] Engage with 5 accounts in your niche
   265|- [ ] Check analytics for unusual activity
   266|
   267|## Weekly (1 hour)
   268|- [ ] Review analytics dashboard
   269|- [ ] Plan next week's content
   270|- [ ] Batch create content
   271|- [ ] Update content calendar
   272|```
   273|
   274|### Content Repurposing Matrix
   275|
   276|| Original | Twitter | LinkedIn | Instagram | Newsletter |
   277||----------|---------|----------|-----------|------------|
   278|| Blog Post | Thread | Summary post | Carousel | Highlight |
   279|| Podcast | Quote tweets | Key insight | Audio clip | Episode notes |
   280|| Video | Clip + thread | Embed | Reel | Behind scenes |
   281|| Thread | - | Expanded post | Story series | Compilation |
   282|
   283|---
   284|
   285|## Brand Voice Guidelines
   286|
   287|### Voice Definition Template
   288|
   289|```markdown
   290|# Brand Voice
   291|
   292|## We Are
   293|- [Trait 1]: [Example]
   294|- [Trait 2]: [Example]
   295|- [Trait 3]: [Example]
   296|
   297|## We Are Not
   298|- [Anti-trait 1]: [Why to avoid]
   299|- [Anti-trait 2]: [Why to avoid]
   300|
   301|## Tone Spectrum
   302|Formal ----[X]---- Casual
   303|Serious ----[X]---- Playful
   304|Reserved ----[X]---- Enthusiastic
   305|
   306|## Sample Phrases
   307|- Instead of "Click here" → "Dive in"
   308|- Instead of "Buy now" → "Start your journey"
   309|- Instead of "We're the best" → "Here's what we learned"
   310|
   311|## Emoji Usage
   312|- Frequency: [Sparingly/Moderate/Freely]
   313|- Favorites: [List emojis that fit brand]
   314|- Never use: [Emojis to avoid]
   315|```
   316|
   317|---
   318|
   319|## Scripts
   320|
   321|### content-calendar.sh
   322|Manage your content calendar from the command line.
   323|
   324|```bash
   325|# Initialize calendar
   326|./scripts/content-calendar.sh init
   327|
   328|# Add content
   329|./scripts/content-calendar.sh add "2024-01-15" "twitter" "Thread on productivity"
   330|
   331|# View week
   332|./scripts/content-calendar.sh week
   333|
   334|# View month
   335|./scripts/content-calendar.sh month
   336|```
   337|
   338|### analytics-report.sh
   339|Generate weekly analytics summaries.
   340|
   341|```bash
   342|# Generate this week's report
   343|./scripts/analytics-report.sh weekly
   344|
   345|# Compare to last week
   346|./scripts/analytics-report.sh compare
   347|```
   348|
   349|---
   350|
   351|## Integration Tips
   352|
   353|### With Other Skills
   354|
   355|| Skill | Integration |
   356||-------|-------------|
   357|| **Data Analyst** | Deeper analytics, trend visualization |
   358|| **Sales** | Align campaigns with sales pipeline |
   359|| **Business Development** | Content for partnerships |
   360|
   361|### Common Workflows
   362|
   363|**Content from Meetings:**
   364|When you have a meeting transcript, extract quotable insights for social content.
   365|
   366|**Analytics to Strategy:**
   367|Use data-analyst skill to visualize marketing performance and identify optimization opportunities.
   368|
   369|---
   370|
   371|## Best Practices
   372|
   373|1. **Consistency > Perfection** — Regular posting beats occasional perfection
   374|2. **80/20 Content Rule** — 80% value, 20% promotion
   375|3. **Engage, Don't Broadcast** — Social is a conversation
   376|4. **Test Everything** — A/B test hooks, CTAs, posting times
   377|5. **Batch Create** — Write a week's content in one focused session
   378|6. **Repurpose Ruthlessly** — One idea, multiple formats
   379|7. **Track What Matters** — Pick 3-5 KPIs, ignore vanity metrics
   380|8. **Stay Authentic** — People follow people, not brands
   381|
   382|---
   383|
   384|## Troubleshooting
   385|
   386|**Low engagement?**
   387|- Check posting times against audience activity
   388|- Review hooks — are they scroll-stopping?
   389|- Increase engagement with others (reciprocity works)
   390|
   391|**Inconsistent posting?**
   392|- Batch create content weekly
   393|- Use scheduling tools
   394|- Create content bank for backup
   395|
   396|**Off-brand content?**
   397|- Review brand voice guidelines
   398|- Create swipe file of good examples
   399|- Check content before posting
   400|
   401|---
   402|
   403|## License
   404|
   405|**License:** MIT — use freely, modify, distribute.
   406|
   407|---
   408|
   409|*"Marketing is no longer about the stuff you make, but about the stories you tell." — Seth Godin*
   410|
   411|---
   412|
   413|# AGENT DIRECTIVE: Execution Protocol
   414|
   415|> **CRITICAL INSTRUCTION FOR ALL MIFECO AGENTS**
   416|
   417|## The Golden Rule
   418|
   419|**DO NOT SUGGEST ACTIONS. EXECUTE THEM.**
   420|
   421|### What This Means
   422|
   423|| ❌ DON'T | ✅ DO |
   424||---------|-------|
   425|| "You could create a file..." | Create the file. |

   427|| "Here's a script you might use..." | Execute the script. |
   428|| "Would you like me to...?" | Just do it and report results. |
   429|
   430|### Execution Standard
   431|
   432|When assigned a task:
   433|
   434|1. **Execute immediately** - Don't ask for permission unless explicitly blocked
   435|2. **Report what you did** - Not what you "would" do
   436|3. **Show results** - Output, files created, changes made
   437|4. **Escalate on failure** - Don't stall, notify immediately
   438|
   439|## Failure Protocol
   440|
   441|If you **CANNOT** perform an action:
   442|
   443|**STEP 1:** Try alternative approaches (max 2 attempts)
   444|
   445|**STEP 2:** If still blocked, send immediate notification:
   446|
   447|```json
   448|{
   449|  "timestamp": "ISO-8601",

   469|🚨 AGENT FAILURE ALERT
   470|
   471|Agent: [your-agent-id]
   472|Task: [task_id]
   473|Error: [specific error]
   474|
   475|Needs: [what is required]
   476|Timestamp: [ISO-8601]

   478|
   479|## Telegram Notification Template
   480|
   481|Use this exact format for Telegram alerts:
   482|

   484|🚨 [AGENT] FAILED: [Brief Task Description]
   485|
   486|Error: [Specific error message]

{"content": "     1|---
     2|name: Content Marketing
     3|slug: content-marketing
     4|version: 1.0.0
     5|homepage: https://clawic.com/skills/content-marketing
     6|description: Plan, create, and distribute content with editorial calendars, funnel strategy, and repurposing workflows.
     7|metadata: {"clawdbot":{"emoji":"📝","requires":{"bins":[]},"os":["linux","darwin","win32"]}}
     8|---
     9|
    10|## Setup
    11|
    12|On first use, read `setup.md` for integration guidelines.
    13|
    14|## When to Use
    15|
    16|User needs help with content strategy, editorial planning, blog posts, social media content, or content distribution. Agent handles calendar management, topic ideation, funnel alignment, and repurposing workflows.
    17|
    18|## Architecture
    19|
    20|With user consent, data is stored locally in `~/content-marketing/`. See `memory-template.md` for structure.
    21|
    22|```
    23|~/content-marketing/
    24|├── memory.md           # Strategy, voice, goals
    25|├── calendar.md         # Editorial calendar
    26|├── content-bank/       # Drafts and ideas
    27|└── analytics/          # Performance notes
    28|```
    29|
    30|**First use:** Ask user for permission before creating this folder. The skill works without storage but cannot remember preferences between sessions.
    31|
    32|## Quick Reference
    33|
    34|| Topic | File |
    35||-------|------|
    36|| Setup process | `setup.md` |
    37|| Memory template | `memory-template.md` |
    38|| Funnel strategy | `funnels.md` |
    39|| Repurposing workflows | `repurposing.md` |
    40|
    41|## Core Rules
    42|
    43|### 1. Align Every Piece to Funnel Stage
    44|Before creating content, identify:
    45|- **TOFU** (Top of Funnel): Awareness, broad topics, SEO-focused
    46|- **MOFU** (Middle): Consideration, comparisons, how-tos
    47|- **BOFU** (Bottom): Decision, case studies, demos, pricing
    48|
    49|Content without funnel alignment wastes effort.
    50|
    51|### 2. One Core Idea, Multiple Formats
    52|Every pillar content piece should generate:
    53|- 1 long-form article or video
    54|- 3-5 social posts
    55|- 1 email newsletter section
    56|- Quote graphics or carousels
    57|
    58|Never create once and forget. Repurpose systematically.
    59|
    60|### 3. Editorial Calendar is Sacred
    61|Track in the editorial calendar:
    62|- Publication dates
    63|- Content type and funnel stage
    64|- Status (idea / draft / review / published)
    65|- Distribution channels
    66|
    67|Review calendar weekly. Gaps in calendar = gaps in pipeline.
    68|
    69|### 4. Voice Consistency
    70|Document brand voice in memory:
    71|- Tone (professional, casual, provocative)
    72|- Words to use and avoid
    73|- Example sentences that nail the voice
    74|
    75|Every piece should sound like the same person wrote it.
    76|
    77|### 5. Distribution > Creation
    78|80% of effort should go to distribution:
    79|- Cross-post to all relevant channels
    80|- Repurpose for each platform's format
    81|- Engage with comments and shares
    82|- Update and republish evergreen content
    83|
    84|Creating content nobody sees is content that doesn't exist.
    85|
    86|### 6. Measure What Matters
    87|Track per content type:
    88|- Traffic and engagement
    89|- Conversion to next funnel stage
    90|- Time on page / completion rate
    91|- Social shares and saves
    92|
    93|Stop producing what doesn't perform.
    94|
    95|### 7. Content Bank Never Empty
    96|Always maintain 10+ ideas in content-bank/:
    97|- Problems your audience has
    98|- Questions they ask
    99|- Trends in your space
   100|- Competitor gaps
   101|
   102|If you run out of ideas, you're not listening enough.
   103|
   104|## Common Traps
   105|
   106|- **No funnel alignment** → Content gets views but no conversions
   107|- **Create and forget** → Single-use content wastes 80% of value
   108|- **Inconsistent voice** → Brand feels fragmented
   109|- **Publishing without distribution plan** → Content dies in silence
   110|- **Chasing trends over evergreen** → Constant treadmill, no compounding
   111|- **Ignoring analytics** → Repeating failures, missing wins
   112|
   113|## Security & Privacy
   114|
   115|**Data that stays local (with user consent):**
   116|- Content strategy and voice preferences in `~/content-marketing/memory.md`
   117|- Editorial calendar in `~/content-marketing/calendar.md`
   118|- Content ideas in `~/content-marketing/content-bank/`
   119|
   120|**This skill does NOT:**
   121|- Send data to external services
   122|- Access files outside `~/content-marketing/`
   123|- Create files without explicit user permission
   124|- Collect or transmit analytics
   125|
   126|**User control:**
   127|- Storage is optional — decline and the skill still works for ideation and advice
   128|- Delete `~/content-marketing/` anytime to remove all stored data
   129|
   130|## Related Skills
   131|Install with `clawhub install <slug>` if user confirms:
   132|- `seo` — Optimize content for search
   133|- `writing` — Craft better copy
   134|- `growth-hacker` — Distribution tactics
   135|- `branding` — Maintain brand consistency
   136|
   137|## Feedback
   138|
   139|- If useful: `clawhub star content-marketing`
   140|- Stay updated: `clawhub sync`
   141|
   142|---
   143|

    41|## Core Rules
    42|
    43|1. **Never force push to shared branches** — Use `--force-with-lease` on feature branches only
    44|2. **Commit early, commit often** — Small commits are easier to review, revert, and bisect
    45|3. **Write meaningful commit messages** — First line under 72 chars, imperative mood
    46|4. **Pull before push** — Always `git pull --rebase` before pushing to avoid merge commits
    47|5. **Clean up before merging** — Use `git rebase -i` to squash fixup commits
    48|
    49|## Team Workflows
    50|
    51|**Feature Branch Flow:**
    52|1. `git checkout -b feature/name` from main
    53|2. Make commits, push regularly
    54|3. Open PR, get review
    55|4. Squash and merge to main
    56|5. Delete feature branch
    57|
    58|**Hotfix Flow:**
    59|1. `git checkout -b hotfix/issue` from main
    60|2. Fix, test, commit
    61|3. Merge to main AND develop (if exists)
    62|4. Tag the release
    63|

    65|```bash

    67|git rebase origin/main  # or merge if team prefers
    68|```

    70|## Commit Messages
    71|
